question: Capodichino airport is located in central Naples, a city which is among the most densely populated in Europe and one long plagued by environmental problems. In 25 years, no optimal initial climb procedure has been enforced in order to limit noise impact in the SID (standard initial departure) phase. The LVA index used does not comply with the ECAC calculation method (ECAC Document 29).

The monitoring units do not comply with the noise indices prescribed by ECAC-ISPRA; there is also non-compliance as regards the types of units installed (A, M, V) and discrepancies between airport acoustic zoning and municipal acoustic classification. Given the above, can the Commission respond to the following questions: 1.

What concrete measures does it intend to take to resolve the lack of an optimal initial climb procedure, the transparency of the AEDT model input database and the non-conformities in noise indices at Naples airport?

How might it help improve compliance with EU regulations at Naples and Salerno airports, in particular with Regulation (EU) No 598/2014 and Regulation (EU) No 139/2014, so as to ensure that the airport management there meets the required standards?

What steps can it take to address the unreconcilable differences in the nature of the runways, conduct a review of the site-specific obstacles and buildings in SIDs and draw up limitation maps and an external emergency plan for Naples airport?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (26.4.

2024) Regulation (EU) No 598/2014 on the establishment of rules and procedures with regard to the introduction of noise-related operating restrictions at Union airports within a Balanced Approach and repealing Directive 2002/30/EC1 (hereafter ‘Balanced Approach Regulation’) requires that Member States’ competent authorities regularly assess the noise situation in accordance with Directive 2002/49/EC relating to the assessment and management of environmental noise2 (hereafter ‘Environmental Noise Directive’) at airports for which they are responsible.

To this end Italy submitted a Noise Action Plan for Capodichino Airport in Naples for the period 2018 to 2023 (extended by one year due to COVID-19) after a public consultation of a duration of 45 days. As required by the Balanced Approach Regulation, the Noise Action Plan identifies noise mitigating measures under the pillars of the balanced approach process, including noise abatement operational procedures.

For example, the Noise Action Plan includes noise mitigating take-off procedures. It should be noted that the enforcement of these measures falls within the remit of Member States rather than Commission. Similarly, the optimisation of take-off and landing procedures is also for national competent authorities to assess and implement.

Regarding the methodology to assess and measure noise, the Environmental Noise Directive allows Member States to use different indicators than those included in the Directive. Member States must notify the Commission of such national indicators and explain how they are implemented. The Commission does not have any indications that the Italian authorities did not transpose the Directive correctly.
